title: Oeufs en Cocotte
subtitle: Baked eggs in cream
excerpt: Eggs baked in small ramekins with cream and a little butter until the whites just set and the yolks stay runny. Ready in 15 minutes and endlessly variable.

recipe.sourceNotes: Oeufs en cocotte are a classic of the French home kitchen and bistro, appearing in cookbooks including Escoffier's Le Guide Culinaire and Elizabeth David's French Provincial Cooking.

content.text: Oeufs en cocotte are eggs baked in buttered ramekins with a splash of cream. The whites set, the yolks stay soft, and the whole thing takes less than 15 minutes in the oven. The base layer can be anything, from a spoonful of leftover ratatouille to smoked salmon or sauteed mushrooms, and the eggs bake on top.
Heat the oven to 180 C / fan 160 C / gas 4. Butter two ramekins generously. Place them in a roasting tin.
Pour 1 tablespoon of cream into each ramekin. Break 2 eggs carefully into each ramekin so the yolks stay whole. Spoon another tablespoon of cream over the top of each. Season with salt and pepper.
Pour boiling water into the roasting tin to come halfway up the sides of the ramekins. Cover the tin loosely with foil.

Bake for 10 to 12 minutes, until the whites are just set and the yolks are still runny. They will continue to cook slightly after they come out of the oven, so pull them a moment before they look done. Scatter over chives and serve with bread.
Smoked salmon: lay a slice in the base before adding the cream and eggs.
Mushroom: fry 80 g sliced mushrooms in a little butter, season, and spoon into the base.
Ham and cheese: put a slice of ham in the base and scatter grated gruyere over the cream before baking.
